name: WordPress
purpose: The CMS the entire bartlettroofs.com website runs on. Every page, post, and location page lives here.
howWeUseIt: All page/content edits happen in WordPress admin, built in Draft and shown in Preview before anything publishes.
The page builder is Avada/Fusion Builder — not Elementor. Global Avada templates affect many pages at once; never bulk-edit one without knowing every page it touches.
A custom post type named 'service-areas' powers the individual city/location pages (e.g. /service-areas/boise-id/).
Yoast (see separate entry) is installed on top of WordPress for SEO fields.
verifiedNotes: Confirmed high-confidence (data/site-facts.json: fact-cms, fact-service-areas-cpt). The full active-plugin list was inventoried once (task ta983d02c21c843f2, done) — see memory/log.md and the dashboard's Archive tab for that snapshot rather than assuming it here.
cautions: Never touch the live site unless explicitly asked — read-only discovery is the default.
Confirm a working, restorable backup exists before any live-site change.
Mikey logs in. Never ask for or handle WordPress or hosting passwords.

name: Yoast SEO
purpose: The SEO plugin controlling page titles, meta descriptions, XML sitemaps, and taxonomy indexing settings for the WordPress site.
howWeUseIt: SEO title + meta description edits for any page happen here (WordPress → Yoast → the page's SEO tab).
The XML sitemap Yoast generates is what gets submitted to Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools.

Yoast's Settings → Content Types / Taxonomies screen controls which taxonomies (e.g. testimonial-tag, element-category) get their own sitemap entries and indexing — utility taxonomies unrelated to real content should be disabled here to avoid wasting crawl budget.
verifiedNotes: Confirmed high-confidence as the SEO plugin in use, not Rank Math (data/site-facts.json: fact-seo-plugin).
cautions: Not Rank Math — don't propose Rank Math-specific instructions.
Verify any schema/meta change in View Source after publishing, not just the Yoast preview.

name: Avada / Fusion Builder
purpose: The visual page-building tool used to lay out every page on the site, including new location and service pages.
howWeUseIt: New pages (Exteriors hub, service pages, location pages) are built by pulling the existing Avada brand tokens/template so they match the rest of the site.
Global Avada templates apply to many pages at once — a change to one propagates everywhere it's used.
verifiedNotes: Confirmed high-confidence as the page builder in use, not Elementor (data/site-facts.json: fact-cms).
cautions: Never bulk-edit an Avada global template without understanding every page it affects.
Build in Draft, show Preview, publish only on approval.

name: Google Search Console
purpose: Google's own index/coverage/ranking data source — what's indexed, what's erroring, what's ranking and for which queries.
howWeUseIt: Weekly: pull the last 7 days for new coverage errors and top gaining/losing pages or queries (see the Technical & Site Health SOP).
Used to confirm which page currently ranks for a given query before doing internal-linking or content work (e.g. the 'roofer near me' URL-targeting fix).
The 'Why pages aren't indexed' report is the primary tool for investigating the 351-of-626-pages-excluded issue.
Provides the submission target for the Yoast XML sitemap, and cross-checks Bing Webmaster Tools coverage.
verifiedNotes: Access confirmed working (task t74893df606e34be5, done) with a 90-day baseline pulled — see memory/log.md for that snapshot. Known tracking gaps remain unverified (data/site-facts.json: fact-tracking-gaps) — treat GSC as reliable for indexing/ranking data but don't assume it reconciles perfectly with GA4/CallRail yet.
cautions: One data pull is a snapshot, not a trend — always compare to the prior week/month before drawing a conclusion.
Confirm which GSC property (with/without www, http/https) is verified before citing numbers.

name: Google Analytics 4 (GA4)
purpose: Primary web analytics/behavior tracking — traffic, conversions, and (once fixed) lead attribution.
howWeUseIt: Weekly: cross-referenced with CallRail and Meta to confirm every lead has source/campaign attribution.
Used with Tag Assistant/DebugView to verify a tracking change actually fires one clean event, rather than assuming a fix worked.
Landing page performance (LCP, conversion rate, cost per lead) is reviewed here monthly alongside PageSpeed Insights and Meta.
verifiedNotes: Access confirmed working with a 90-day baseline pulled (task t74893df606e34be5, done). A suspected double-fire (GA4 firing via both Site Kit and GTM simultaneously, inflating numbers) is an open Discovery task — treat current GA4 volume numbers as potentially overstated until that's resolved (data/site-facts.json: fact-tracking-gaps).
cautions: Never change GA4 tracking or event/form destinations without explicit approval.
Verify with DebugView/a real test lead — don't assume a tracking change worked.

name: Google Tag Manager (GTM)
purpose: Tag/trigger management layer sitting in front of GA4, the Meta Pixel, and other tracking scripts.
howWeUseIt: The likely source of the suspected GA4 double-fire (GA4 firing via both Site Kit and GTM) — GTM is the presumed single source of truth to keep once that's resolved.
Used to fire GA4, Meta Pixel, and CallRail tags on new ad landing pages, along with a defined UTM convention.
verifiedNotes: Existence/use inferred from the GA4 de-dupe task and ads tracking tasks — the exact current tag/trigger configuration has not been audited yet. Treat as an open Discovery item, not a confirmed-clean setup.
cautions: Never change GTM tags/triggers/destinations without explicit approval.
One change at a time; verify via Tag Assistant after each change.

name: Bing Webmaster Tools
purpose: Bing's equivalent of Search Console — index coverage on Bing, and relevant to Microsoft/Copilot-style discovery.
howWeUseIt: Account creation and sitemap submission (the Yoast XML sitemap URL) is a one-time setup task, followed up ~2 weeks later to check coverage.
verifiedNotes: Not yet set up as of the last known status — this is an open task (t70b3e78f599c450c), not a live/confirmed account.
cautions: Treat Bing as one important index source, not a guaranteed ChatGPT/Copilot citation lever.

name: Semrush
purpose: Competitor research, keyword-gap analysis, backlink auditing, and domain authority tracking.
howWeUseIt: Monthly: re-pull domain_rank, domain_organic (top 50), domain_organic_organic, and a keyword-gap batch, compared against the prior baseline.
The Backlink Audit / Backlinks report is used to identify and export confirmed spam/toxic referring domains (filtered by known spam anchor-text patterns) for a Google Search Console disavow file.
Initial full pull completed June 2026 — that data lives in Bartlett-SEO-Intelligence.html on the Desktop, not in this repo.
verifiedNotes: Confirmed in active use (data/tasks.json: monthly Semrush cadence item, disavow-file task). The Backlink Audit toxicity tool is UI-only, not API-accessible — exports must be pulled manually.
cautions: A human must review the disavow domain list before it's ever submitted to Google — never auto-submit.

name: CallRail
purpose: Call tracking with dynamic phone numbers, used to attribute inbound calls to their source/campaign.
howWeUseIt: Weekly lead-review checks that GA4/CallRail/Meta attribution lines up for every new lead.
Part of the tracking stack wired into ad landing pages alongside GA4 and the Meta Pixel.
verifiedNotes: Confirmed part of the real lead-flow stack (data/site-facts.json: fact-lead-stack), but the exact current wiring is an open Discovery task (mapping where contact/quote forms submit).
cautions: Never use a CallRail dynamic tracking number as the public GBP/citation NAP phone number — this is a hard rule, not a style preference.

name: Birdeye
purpose: Manages Google Business Profile (GBP) listings, review requests, and review replies across every market/office.
howWeUseIt: Weekly: check for new reviews on Google + Birdeye, draft replies for Mikey's approval, flag anything needing a phone call.
Monthly: pull new-review count + average rating per location against the 8-12/mo target; adjust ask timing/channel if a market is behind pace.
NAP/category/hours audits and updates go through here — Birdeye is the single place GBP listings get edited.
verifiedNotes: Confirmed already owned/in use (data/tasks.json: 'Birdeye (already owned)'). The automated review-request-on-job-completion configuration and the per-market baseline are open build tasks, not yet live.
cautions: Draft replies for approval — do not post without sign-off, especially for negative reviews.
Never use a CallRail number as the listed NAP phone number here.

name: Meta Business Manager
purpose: Manages Facebook/Instagram ad campaigns, the Meta Pixel, and domain verification for ad landing pages.
howWeUseIt: Ad landing pages in /lp/ get the Meta Pixel wired in alongside GA4 and CallRail, with a defined UTM convention.
Domain verification for the ad landing-page domain has to be completed here before some ad features work.
verifiedNotes: The landing-page build and tracking-wiring tasks (t{e2605450...}, t{f2104dbec...}) are open/not yet built — this is the intended architecture, not a confirmed-live setup.
cautions: Meta domain verification and pixel wiring require Mikey to complete the actual steps in Meta Business Manager — an agent can guide, not log in on his behalf.
Never invent stats, service areas, or claims in ad copy — if a number isn't verified, don't use it.

name: Roofle
purpose: Instant roofing-quote tool embedded on the site, generating leads directly.
howWeUseIt: One of the forms whose destination is being mapped in the open lead-flow-mapping task — where Roofle submissions actually land (CRM, email, or otherwise) is not yet fully confirmed.
verifiedNotes: Confirmed part of the real lead-flow stack (data/site-facts.json: fact-lead-stack), but exact wiring is unverified/open (task t7bc1058ff4294488, currently in progress).
cautions: Do not assume Roofle leads are reaching a tracked destination until the lead-flow map confirms it.

name: Gravity Forms
purpose: The WordPress plugin powering the site's contact and quote forms.
howWeUseIt: Same open question as Roofle — the lead-flow-mapping task documents notification emails, CRM/Zapier links, and CallRail/Roofle embedding for every form on the site.
verifiedNotes: Confirmed part of the real lead-flow stack (data/site-facts.json: fact-lead-stack). Exact form-by-form destination wiring is unverified/open.
cautions: Flag any form sending leads only to a personal inbox with no record — that's a real risk, not a hypothetical.

name: SalesTrak
purpose: The CRM sales reps use to pin leads on a map, move jobs through Insurance/Cash workflows, and track everything from first contact through invoicing/A-R.
howWeUseIt: Every lead becomes a pin/project in SalesTrak (Map → Add Project), tagged Residential/Commercial, Inbound/Self-Gen, with a Stage (Observed Damage / No Visible Damage / Aged Roof) and a Lead Source.
Jobs move through the Leads workflow, then automatically or manually into Insurance Jobs or Cash Jobs stages, then Approvals, then the post-sale Scheduling/Production/Invoicing/A-R stages.
Rooflink integration: moving a job into 'Inspection Scheduled' should auto-create it in Rooflink; if that doesn't happen, move the job back one stage and retry.

Marketing's interest in SalesTrak is primarily the Lead Source field (attribution) and the Lost Leads workflow (Not Interested / Interested in the Future / Not Enough Damage) — these should reconcile with GA4/CallRail/Meta attribution, not contradict it.
verifiedNotes: Documented in detail in the separate Sales Representative SOP (Salestrak Desktop SOP.pdf, provided by Mikey). That SOP is the sales-team source of truth for SalesTrak procedure; this entry only summarizes the parts marketing needs to know for lead-source reconciliation.
cautions: Marketing should read SalesTrak's Lead Source / Lost Leads data as a cross-check on attribution, not edit sales-side workflow stages directly.
See the full Sales Representative SOP for anything beyond attribution reconciliation — don't duplicate sales-process detail here.
sourceNote: Salestrak Desktop SOP.pdf (provided by Mikey, 2026-07-15), data/site-facts.json (fact-lead-stack)

name: n8n / Zapier
purpose: Automation/integration glue connecting forms, CRM, and notification tools together.
howWeUseIt: Exact workflows (which automations exist, what they connect) are part of the open lead-flow-mapping task — document any CRM/Zapier link found for each form.
verifiedNotes: Confirmed part of the real lead-flow stack (data/site-facts.json: fact-lead-stack). No specific workflow has been confirmed/documented yet.
cautions: Don't assume an automation exists or works until the lead-flow map confirms it.
